sections.overview: The giant anteater is the largest living anteater, native to Central and South America.
sections.identification: A tubular snout, bushy tail and strong foreclaws distinguish this ground-dwelling species.
sections.habitat: It uses forests, wetlands, savannas and other open habitats across its range.
sections.diet: It feeds mainly on ants and termites, collected with its long sticky tongue.
sections.behavior: It is usually solitary and diurnal, walking on its knuckles to protect its claws.
sections.reproduction: After roughly six months, a female usually gives birth to one young that rides on her back.
sections.ecology: By eating ants and termites, it influences local insect communities.
sections.conservation: The IUCN Anteater, Sloth and Armadillo Specialist Group reports the species as Vulnerable, citing habitat loss and fragmentation, fires and road deaths among its threats.
